books.section: Topic 2.5 Interactions Between American Indians and Europeans
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.misconception: Leadership disputes among Pueblo leaders were not the motive Josephe describes.
options.text: A dispute among Pueblo leaders over who would govern once the Spanish were expelled.

options.misconception: Reopening trade routes was not the cause; daily abuses were.
options.text: A desire to reopen the pre-contact trade routes that Spanish missions had closed off.

options.misconception: No English military aid figured in the Pueblo revolt.
options.text: Promises of military aid from English colonists on the Atlantic coast.
Specific daily abuses: beatings, seizure of their property, and forced labor without pay.

rationales.A: Leadership disputes among Pueblo leaders were not the motive Josephe describes.
rationales.B: Reopening trade routes was not the cause; daily abuses were.
rationales.C: No English military aid figured in the Pueblo revolt.
rationales.D: Josephe is specific, and his specifics are physical: Spanish officials beat the Pueblo people, seized their property, and forced them to work without pay. These were not abstract grievances but daily abuses — the kind of suffering that makes people risk everything. The revolt began in the body, in beatings and stolen goods and unpaid labor, before it became a war over gods and churches.
rationales.general:
1. Read what Josephe actually says. Beatings, seized property, and forced labor without pay.
2. Ask what kind of grievances those are. Daily and physical, not abstract or distant.
3. Name the motive. The revolt began in the body before it became a war over gods and churches.
Remember: when a witness lists specifics, trust the list — it is the motive.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from the 1681 interrogation of Josephe
stem: Josephe's testimony indicates that the Pueblo rebels' motives centered most directly on which of the following?

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the 1681 interrogation of Josephe.
stimulus.text: Asked what drove the rebels to renounce Spanish authority, Josephe — a Spanish-speaking Pueblo Indian questioned by colonial officials after the 1680 uprising — answered that the causes were the ill treatment they suffered: Spanish officials beat them, seized their property, and forced them to work without pay. Asked why the rebels burned churches and images, mocked sacred objects, and killed priests, Josephe said he had heard it stated that while besieging the Spanish villa the rebels shouted that the Spaniards' God was dead and that only their own gods lived. Their captains ordered that the names of Jesus and Mary never be spoken, and Josephe reported seeing new houses of native worship built where the people danced their traditional ceremonial dances. — paraphrased from the 1681 interrogation of Josephe
